commands.command: is right, and i need to retract a specific claim i made above. i wrote that the docs "name the paths that still cancel and keep history: provider throw, missing model, missing credentials." a configured provider that throws is **not** one of them. ```js } catch (err) { // caller cancellation and real transport timeouts remain terminal. if (signal?.aborted || (!isaborterror(err) && istimeouterror(err))) throw err; log.warn(`compaction provider "${compactionprovider.id}" failed, falling back to llm: ...`); } ``` the exception is caught and execution continues into built-in llm summarization. enumerating the terminal sites at the reviewed head confirms it from the other direction - four cancel sites, and a provider throw is in none of them: | site | reason | |---|---| | `:1239` | could not resolve a summarization model | | `:1248` | `authresult.reason` (credentials) | | `:1411` | finalized summary failed quality checks and corrective generation failed | | `:1528` | could not summarize the session | so all three pages named a path that cannot happen, and `docs/reference/session-management-compaction.md` contradicted itself: line 254 said a provider throw cancels while line 255 already documented the fallback. one refinement on the suggested wording. "say that a failed built-in generation after fallback is terminal instead" is right but incomplete - a caller-initiated abort and a real transport timeout **are** re-thrown, per the guard above. all three pages now say: provider throw or empty result falls back to built-in summarization; a failed built-in generation, an unresolvable model, and missing credentials cancel and keep history; aborts and transport timeouts are re-thrown. ## both nits from @hansen1018 **test naming.** renamed to `retains the generated split-turn section when a final audit failure degrades to the fallback`, so the title matches the in-test comment. **a dedicated test for `degradetofallbacksummary`.** i did not extract it, and i want to be explicit about the tradeoff rather than quietly skip it. it is a closure over seven bindings (`log`, `finalizesummarytext`, `buildstructuredfallbacksummary`, `effectiveprevioussummary`, `splitturnsectionlocal`, `preservedturnssectionlocal`, `producerlosses`). extracting it means parameter plumbing on a production file whose diff size is already flagged as a merge risk in this review. instead i went looking for what was actually unguarded, and found a real gap: `degrades when audit-required tail sections cannot fit the artifact cap` sets `issplitturn: false` and `recentturnspreserve: 0`, so it never checked composition. **only the audit path was protected.** the new test drives the *retention* path with a split turn and asserts the same artifact composition, which is the "single fallback owner" property both reviews care about. ### evidence `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` ``` before tests 139 passed (139) after tests 140 passed (140) exit 0 ``` mutation-checked, restored byte-identical (`sha256 45f7fc5ebe00ba75`): | mutation | result | |---|---| | drop `generatedsplitturnsection` from the degraded path | **2 failed** / 138 passed, exit 1 | | restored | 140 passed, exit 0 | that mutation failed **one** test before this commit and fails **two** after it, on both terminal entry points - which is the coverage claim, stated as a measurement rather than an assertion. run on node 24.18.0, matching the version this repo's ci pins. ## not done in this push **the rebase (p1) is still outstanding.** it is not mechanical. `upstream/main` has moved 3640 commits since this branch's merge-base, and `96843f9a725` (#132449) renamed `setcompactionsafeguardcancelreason` to `setcompactionsafeguardcancellation` - the very area this pr touches. a trial rebase conflicts on the first of three commits in both `compaction-safeguard.ts` and its test. that is a re-derivation against restructured semantics, and i would rather do it as its own reviewable step than fold a hasty conflict resolution into a review-response push. worth noting for whoever picks it up: upstream still cancels on `qualityretentioninfeasible` (`compaction-safeguard.ts:1386-1390`), and has zero occurrences of `degradetofallbacksummary` or `quality_guard_degraded_fallback` - so this pr has not been superseded. **linking #120162** as @hansen1018 suggested - *qualityguard audit retry shares the `timeoutseconds` budget and is killed by the same abort signal*. confirmed still open, and it is the same code path. if the collective watchdog fires rather than per attempt, retries are exhausted for a reason unrelated to summary quality, and the session then lands in `quality_guard_degraded_fallback` with a misleading diagnostic. this pr makes that outcome survivable instead of terminal, which is strictly better, but the two should be read together. claude assisted with the patch and this comment. the submitter owns the conclusions and final review.
